ratings_why.fun: Setting each Lid's N against your knock sources is a real drafting puzzle with two opposite endgames, but permanent growth stops at Tier 4, so the late board grows only inside fights.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because a Lid changes who can be hit, which front row counts and who attacks first, mid-fight and on your own schedule, and it hides your board from scouting; no tribe today touches those rules.

verdict_why: v2 closed the rules gaps; what is left is balance for the owner to watch, not a fix.

points.text: Permanent growth peaks at the Inner Guard (Tier 4); Tiers 5 and 6 are all in-fight. One late card that grows Lids permanently, such as a Keeper of Aprons effect without the twice-a-fight cap, would give the late game a growing board to watch.

Grit-Dresser knocks one at a time, so with three empty slots Brother Atypus can spring, kill, retreat and spring again three times at Start of Combat, before the enemy acts. A great payoff; worth simulating with goldens.
The Long Wait leaves many unsprung Lids that count for hero damage without ever taking a risk. The design's own fallback, counting only face-up survivors, is ready if it hits too hard.
Grand Tyler: say plainly that the fight copy attacks at once, as a spring does, so players don't wonder whether it waits as a Lid.

standouts.why: Stab, hide, stab again is the seed's fantasy in one card, and the golden is a high roll worth chasing.
Turns empty slots into a resource and makes the standing trade-off, a knock or a missing unit, a real choice every turn.
A Tier 6 capstone that points the tribe the opposite way from the Worshipful Master: never spring, then spring all at once.

weakest.why: A plain 3/3 whose knocks come only when it attacks, often after the moment the Lids needed them.
Small, positional Tier 2 buffer that the Inner Guard replaces outright two tiers later.
A 1/4 that does nothing in the fight; 1 gold a turn is fine, but only in the Long Wait build.

flags.note: With Grit-Dresser knocks, a buffed or golden Atypus can clear several enemies before they act; high Health, Shield and Bristle are the counters.
With Old Diadem and Ashby's Nieces, springs per fight can reach the teens, so +1/+1 per spring to every unit could run well past Tier 6's in-fight target.
A Discover every turn once knocks make her spring reliably is strong Tier 4 economy.
Unsprung Lids count as surviving units, so Long Wait wins can deal heavy hero damage.
